purpose: The migration contract. For each competing gateway SDK, exactly which inputs Conifer HONORS, which it TRANSLATES, and which it REFUSES to pretend about. A field this card marks `unsupported` is one the shim throws on rather than dropping silently — dropping a routing or spend constraint is the failure mode that makes a migration look successful and bill wrong.
law: Never silently drop a constraint. A ceiling, a venue, or a provider restriction that cannot be honored is an error at the call site, not an absence at the gateway.
Never invent a server feature client-side and present it as one. Client-side chains report themselves as client-side (`fallbackIndex`, `x-conifer-client`).
Model ids migrate untouched. `vendor/model` resolves through the gateway's own last-segment rule; the SDK does no rewriting of its own.

honored.response_format: forwarded verbatim to the upstream; honored where the upstream honors it

translated.models: OpenRouter's fallback array. The gateway admits exactly one model per request, so the SDK walks the array as a CLIENT-SIDE chain and reports `fallbackIndex`. Opt in with `allowClientFallback: true`; without it the shim throws rather than quietly serving only the first.
translated.usage.cost: OpenRouter returns credits on the body. Conifer discloses nanodollars on `x-conifer-cost-nanousd`, which is exact integer money. The shim exposes both `costNanoUsd` and a `usage.cost`-shaped USD number computed from it.
translated.transforms: [\"middle-out\"]: no server-side prompt compression exists here. The shim throws; it will not ship a silently-different prompt.
translated.HTTP-Referer / X-Title: mapped to `x-conifer-client` (usage attribution). Conifer has no public app-ranking board, so this is attribution only.

unsupported_refused.provider: OpenRouter's ProviderPreferences (order/allow_fallbacks/ignore/data_collection/quantizations). Conifer picks the host for the admitted model by price/health inside the gateway; a client cannot pin it. Sending this throws.
unsupported_refused.route: `route: "fallback"` is server-side failover. Conifer admits exactly the model you name, so there is no host-level retry to enable. Use `models` + `allowClientFallback`.
unsupported_refused.prompt: the legacy text-completions field. Conifer serves the chat wire. Throws.
unsupported_refused.top_k / min_p / top_a / repetition_penal: not modelled on the gateway's request card; forwarded ONLY when `passthroughUnknown: true` is set, and then explicitly at the caller's risk.

openrouter.generation_stats_endpoint: OpenRouter's GET /api/v1/generation has no equivalent: Conifer settles the cost onto the SAME response's receipt headers, so the stats are already in hand when the call returns. The shim reads them there rather than making a second call.

vercel_ai_gateway.auth: Vercel accepts an API key OR an OIDC token on the same Bearer header. Conifer accepts an entitlement token or an API key on that same header, so an `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`-shaped integration only changes the value and the URL.

honored.GET /models: identical shape; Conifer adds caps/pricing/endpoint_kind fields that a Vercel-shaped reader ignores
honored.reasoning: the gateway forwards a `reasoning` block and relays vendor reasoning fields on the message; not every model emits one

translated.@ai-sdk/openai-compatible: the supported AI SDK path. `createOpenAICompatible({ baseURL: 'https://api.conifer.build/v1', apiKey })` works unchanged; the SDK ships `coniferAiSdk()` as that call with the base URL and headers pre-wired.
translated.@ai-sdk/gateway (the first-party `gatewa: Vercel-specific transport. Use the openai-compatible provider above instead.
translated.providerOptions.gateway.order: provider pinning — same refusal as OpenRouter's `provider`. Throws.
translated.providerOptions.gateway.models: model fallbacks — same treatment as OpenRouter's `models`: client-side chain, opt-in.

unsupported_refused.POST /embeddings: the gateway serves no embeddings door today. Throws with that sentence, rather than 404-ing from inside the OpenAI client.
unsupported_refused.OIDC auto-auth: there is no Conifer OIDC exchange; supply CONIFER_API_KEY.

helicone.shape: Helicone is a header-driven proxy in front of YOUR provider key. Conifer is the biller and router itself, so the mapping is mostly header-to-header, with the proxy-target headers dropped by definition.

honored.Helicone-Property-*: -> merged into the `x-conifer-client` attribution string; Conifer stores no arbitrary custom-property index, so the shim keeps them client-side for your own logs rather than claiming server storage
honored.Helicone-Cache-Enabled: false: -> `x-conifer-cache: off`, the gateway's real per-request prompt-cache OPT-OUT. Note the asymmetry, which the shim preserves: the header can only turn caching OFF. `Helicone-Cache-Enabled: true` therefore throws — house policy already decides when to cache, and a client cannot force a cache-write class it did not pay for.

translated.Helicone-Auth: -> `Authorization: Bearer $CONIFER_API_KEY`. There is no second credential: Conifer is not proxying your provider key. If you WANT your own provider key used, that is BYOK custody (PUT /v1/keys/{provider}), which the SDK exposes as `keys.put()`.
translated.Helicone-Target-URL / Helicone-OpenAI-Ap: dropped by definition — Conifer is the destination, not a pass-through proxy. Sending one throws so a migrated app cannot believe it is still proxying elsewhere.
translated.Helicone-Fallbacks: -> client-side `fallbackModels`, same opt-in rule as OpenRouter's `models`.
translated.Helicone-RateLimit-Policy: no per-request client-set policy. Conifer's spend control is the HARD `x-conifer-max-cost-nanousd` ceiling, which is strictly stronger (money, not request count). The shim maps a `u=cents` policy onto that ceiling and throws on `u=requests`.
translated.Helicone-Retry-Enabled + helicone-retry-: -> the SDK's own `maxRetries`, which retries ONLY transport faults and 429/502/503/504, always under one idempotency key.

unsupported_refused.Helicone-Moderations-Enabled / Helicone-: no moderation or injection-scanning layer. Throws — a security feature that silently does nothing is worse than an error.
unsupported_refused.Helicone-Token-Limit-Exception-Handler: no server-side truncation or middle-out. The gateway refuses an over-window request with a typed 400 naming the window instead. Throws.
unsupported_refused.Helicone-Session-Id / Session-Path / Ses: no session tree in Conifer's observability. Throws.

receipt_superset.note: What Conifer gives that none of the three do on the response of the SAME call: exact integer nanodollar cost, itemized across the four billed token classes, plus the requested-vs-effective model spelling and the serving endpoint. `costComponentsNanoUsd` always sums to `costNanoUsd`; when that identity cannot be guaranteed the header is omitted rather than approximated.
